--- title: "dsOMOP — Exercises (Solutions)" format: html: code-copy: true execute: warning: false message: false error: true --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DSI); library(DSOpal); library(dsBaseClient); library(dsOMOPClient) builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder() for (s in c("nairobi", "douala", "dakar")) builder$append(server = s, url = paste0("https://", s, ".datashield.live"), user = "ethiopia", password = "P@ssw0rd", profile = "omop") conns <- DSI::datashield.login(logins = builder$build()) ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop_demo.mimic", symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ``` ::: # Exercise 1 — A new numeric variable ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_tbl(ds.omop.column.stats("measurement", "value_as_number", concept_id = 21492239, scope = "pooled", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)$pooled) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| x| |----:| | 8365| | x| |--------:| | 115.1706| | x| |--------:| | 21.79551|
::: ```{.r .cell-code} h <- ds.omop.value.histogram("measurement", value_col = "value_as_number", concept_id = 21492239, symbol = "omop", conns = conns) bins <- do.call(rbind, h$per_site) bins <- subset(bins, !is.na(count)) bins <- aggregate(count ~ bin_start, data = bins, FUN = sum) bins <- bins[order(bins$bin_start), ] barplot(bins$count, names.arg = round(bins$bin_start), las = 2, col = "#4C72B0", border = NA, xlab = "Systolic BP (mmHg)", ylab = "records", main = "Systolic blood pressure") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](omop_exercises_solution_files/figure-html/e1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: > **Answer.** Systolic blood pressure is roughly **symmetric** (mean ≈ median, ~115–120 mmHg), with a **wider spread** than heart rate (sd ≈ 22 vs ≈ 19). A broad-but-symmetric distribution is typical of blood pressure. # Exercise 2 — A new categorical variable ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rh <- ds.omop.value.counts("observation", "value_as_concept_id", concept_id = 40766231, symbol = "omop", conns = conns) show_tbl(rh$per_site$nairobi) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |value | n| n_persons|concept_name | |:--------|--:|---------:|:-------------| |45881671 | 40| 10|Never married | |45883711 | 25| 5|Widowed | |45876756 | 25| 10|Married | |45883375 | 0| 0|Divorced | ::: ::: > **Answer.** The most common status is **Never married**, followed by **Married** and **Widowed**. Some categories are suppressed on this ~100-patient cohort (small-cell control). # Exercise 3 — Find a concept yourself ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} show_tbl(ds.omop.concept.search("hyperlipidemia", domain = "Condition", symbol = "omop", conns = conns)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ::: > **Answer.** Hyperlipidemia is **`concept_id = 432867`**, present in about **45** of the ~100 patients — one of the most common conditions in this ICU cohort. # Exercise 4 — Build your own recipe ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age"), omop_variable(table = "measurement", concept_id = 21492239, format = "mean", name = "systolic_bp"), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 432867, format = "binary", name = "hyperlipidemia")), outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec, out = c(study = "D"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ds.colnames("D", datasources = conns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> $nairobi #> [1] "person_id" "systolic_bp" "hyperlipidemia" "sex" #> [5] "age" #> #> $douala #> [1] "person_id" "systolic_bp" "hyperlipidemia" "sex" #> [5] "age" #> #> $dakar #> [1] "person_id" "systolic_bp" "hyperlipidemia" "sex" #> [5] "age" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ds.dim("D", datasources = conns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> $`dimensions of D in nairobi` #> [1] 35 5 #> #> $`dimensions of D in douala` #> [1] 25 5 #> #> $`dimensions of D in dakar` #> [1] 40 5 #> #> $`dimensions of D in combined studies` #> [1] 100 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ds.summary("D$systolic_bp", datasources = conns)[[1]][["quantiles & mean"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> 5% 10% 25% 50% 75% 90% 95% Mean #> 99.72277 104.13354 112.25500 120.19672 128.68355 133.01607 142.95000 120.33293 ``` ::: ::: > **Answer.** `D` has one row per patient with `sex`, `age`, `systolic_bp`, `hyperlipidemia` (plus `person_id`); ~100 patients combined, mean systolic BP near 120 mmHg. # Exercise 5 — Filter at extraction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec_old <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age"), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 432867, format = "binary", name = "hyperlipidemia")), filters = list(older = omop_filter_age(min = 60)), outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec_old, out = c(study = "D_old"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) ds.dim("D_old", datasources = conns) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> $`dimensions of D_old in nairobi` #> [1] 23 4 #> #> $`dimensions of D_old in douala` #> [1] 13 4 #> #> $`dimensions of D_old in dakar` #> [1] 31 4 #> #> $`dimensions of D_old in combined studies` #> [1] 67 4 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ds.summary("D_old$age", datasources = conns)[[1]][["quantiles & mean"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> 5% 10% 25% 50% 75% 90% 95% Mean #> 60.00000 60.20000 65.00000 74.00000 81.50000 89.60000 92.70000 74.56522 ``` ::: ::: > **Answer.** The filter is applied **during** extraction, so the servers only build patients aged 60+. The cohort shrinks and the minimum age is now 60. # Exercise 6 — A model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rec_h <- omop_recipe( variables = list( omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id", format = "sex_mf", name = "sex"), omop_variable_age(name = "age"), omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence", concept_id = 432867, format = "binary", name = "hyperlipidemia")), outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide")) recipe_execute(rec_h, out = c(study = "H"), symbol = "omop", conns = conns) fit <- ds.glm("H$hyperlipidemia ~ H$age + H$sex", family = "binomial", datasources = conns) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} co <- fit$coefficients show_tbl(data.frame( term = rownames(co), OR = round(co[, "P_OR"], 2), CI_low = round(co[, "low0.95CI.P_OR"], 2), CI_high = round(co[, "high0.95CI.P_OR"], 2), p_value = signif(co[, "p-value"], 3), row.names = NULL)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |term | OR| CI_low| CI_high| p_value| |:-----------|----:|------:|-------:|--------:| |(Intercept) | 0.01| 0.00| 0.08| 6.98e-05| |H$age | 1.07| 1.04| 1.11| 4.43e-05| |H$sexM | 0.99| 0.40| 2.42| 9.75e-01| ::: ::: > **Answer.** **age** is a strong, significant predictor of hyperlipidemia (odds rise with age, p < 0.001) — clinically sensible, since cholesterol problems accumulate over a lifetime. **sex** is not significant. A clean, honest single-predictor result. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} DSI::datashield.logout(conns) ``` :::
